ai.title: Tencent Open-Sources DFly2: Speculative Decoding That Reuses the Target’s Sparse KV Cache
ai.brief: Tencent has open-sourced DFly2 , a speculative decoding drafter built for natively sparse LLMs. 3-Flash and Tencent’s own Hy4 flash . Its main approach is that the drafter keeps no KV cache of its own. This is important for long-context and agentic serving, where draft memory competes with concurrency. 85B-parameter, 5-layer drafter shipped with Hy4 flash. Runs on: Serving tests used NVIDIA H20 GPUs with vLLM, TP8 per instance. Hy4 flash’s vLLM recipe defaults to 8x H200. Performance: Higher draft acceptance than same-recipe DFlash and DSpark on all 3 targets and all general benchmarks. 1-Flash (SWE 64K), at matched per-user speed. 9% over DSpark at temperature 0. What is DFly2? DFly2 is a block-parallel speculative decoding drafter from Tencent’s Hunyuan AI Infra team. It is described in the research paper ‘ DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target’s Sparsity ‘.

sec.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
sec.brief: Details have emerged about a new zero-day vulnerability in Cacti, an open-source network monitoring tool, that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution. The proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, which has yet to be assigned a CVE identifier, has been tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT.
